content.comment_body: Good morning everyone. I can't get my microSD card to be recognized by my [product_name] ([article_no]). I've tried two Kingston microSD cards (one 4GB and one 16GB), formatted them in FAT32 with several cluster sizes and a slow format. None of this worked; whenever I download the program using [product_name], I receive an error stating the microSD isn't responding. Even accessing the microSD directly from the device shows it's not responding. I’ve also ordered a SanDisk microSD to try. Are there any other tests you recommend? Thanks!

Hello [user_name], welcome to the forum. I use different microSD cards from various manufacturers and most capacities (2GB to 32GB, even a partitioned 64GB), and haven’t had any problems. Are you sure the microSD is inserted in the correct direction? It’s possible the card slot pins might be bent.
I’m confident I inserted the microSD card correctly. My [product_name] is new. Could it be defective? Do you have any other possible insights?

Just to confirm: - You formatted the microSD card to FAT32. - The size is appropriate. - You used a slow format. Have you checked the diagnostics menu of the [product_name]? What does it display? Main menu > diagnostic > Hardware > SD card
In the diagnostic menu, my [product_name] says: 'Micro SD Card: Read error'.

It seems there’s an issue either with the mSD card or the card slot. I can’t provide further advice. As mentioned, I haven’t had problems with microSD cards on my [product_name] devices. You may want to submit a support request.

I found an older 8GB Kingston card, and it worked successfully in my [product_name]. For this card, I prepared it using Linux by deleting partitions and formatting to FAT32. If you’re limited to a Windows PC, try using the SD Memory Card Formatter to prepare your card.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are facing persistent problems with microSD card recognition on the [product_name] ([version_no], [article_no]). Despite using multiple brands and trying various formatting approaches like FAT32 and different cluster sizes, the device does not read any microSD cards, resulting in a 'Read error.' This occurs even with new hardware and standard setups, indicating possible compatibility, hardware, or documentation limitations disrupting the intended functionality.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [product_name] ([version_no]) to consistently recognize and interact with properly formatted microSD cards to allow for basic program management and operations.
